# Getting help

## Where to ask

| Your question | Best place |
| --- | --- |
| "Is there an open-source tool for X?" | [Discussions → Q&A](https://github.com/orgs/open-cheme-hub/discussions/categories/q-a) |
| "This template throws an error" | Issue on [`templates`](https://github.com/open-cheme-hub/templates/issues) |
| "The Snakemake workflow fails at rule Y" | Issue on [`workflows`](https://github.com/open-cheme-hub/workflows/issues) |
| "This link is dead / goes somewhere else now" | Issue on the list repo, or just fix it in a PR |
| "How do I add a resource?" | [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) |
| "Can you help debug my Aspen model?" | Not us — try [Eng-Tips](https://www.eng-tips.com/) or [r/ChemicalEngineering](https://reddit.com/r/ChemicalEngineering) |
| "Do my homework" | Also not us, though `templates/` is a legitimate head start |

## What we can and can't help with

**We can** point you at tools, explain how our templates and workflows are meant to be used, fix
our own bugs, and argue productively about which library is right for a job.

**We can't** provide engineering advice you'd act on for a real plant, review your design, validate
a safety case, or take responsibility for results produced with anything here. Everything in this
organisation is reference material. A licensed engineer signs off on real work; that is not a
formality we can shortcut for you.

## Making a good bug report

Include the four things that decide whether anyone can help:

1. **What you ran** — the exact command or notebook cell.
2. **What happened** — the full traceback, pasted as text in a code block, not a screenshot.
3. **What you expected** instead.
4. **Your environment** — OS, Python version, and `conda list` / `pip freeze` for the relevant
   packages. If you used our Docker image, its tag.

A minimal reproducing case beats a long description almost every time.

## Response times

Volunteers, mostly practising engineers and researchers. Expect a reply within a week, slower
around conference deadlines and semester starts. Nudging a quiet thread is fine.
